transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. This is not a DIY job for you to fix yourself. Because this involves gas components inside the appliance, any repair must be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer. However, I can tell you what is likely happening so you know what to expect when they arrive. The symptom of the flame lighting but dying as soon as you release the knob is almost always caused by one of two things: 1. A dirty or misaligned burner cap: If the metal disc over the flame was wet, greasy, or not seated perfectly flat after cleaning, it can prevent the flame from reaching the sensor.
2. A faulty Flame Failure Device (FFD): This is a safety probe that detects the flame. If it is cold, dirty, or failing, it tells the gas valve to shut off because it 'thinks' there is no fire. Before you call an engineer, please check this one simple thing: Look at the burner inside the oven (the part where the flame comes out). Is the metal cap sitting perfectly flat and dry? If it looks wet or slightly tilted, try lifting it off, wiping it completely dry, and placing it back on so it sits flush. Try lighting the oven again. Does it stay lit now? If it still goes out, please do not attempt any further repairs.

I had a look and can't see anything out of place, it seems to be sitting properly, but it still goes out when I let go. I do get a brief whiff of gas while I'm trying to light it, which clears quickly, and the CO alarm in the kitchen hasn't gone off. What should I do next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Flame failure device (FFD) / thermocouple not sensing flame (high)

plan: They asked: "Is this a DIY job?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Richmond.
The fault they reported is: "oven flame goes out when knob is released". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (gas work): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
